literal: This is this minister's aim.
idiomatic: This is what your minister seeks.

literal: An edict entrusted it to the relevant offices; their memorials of deliberation differed.
idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the relevant offices; their deliberations failed to agree.

literal: Xiaoyou spoke again: "Nowadays men are born as slaves and bondsmen, yet their funerals rival those of kings and marquises; living and dead follow different paths, and restraint is gone.
idiomatic: Xiaoyou spoke again: "Today men are born bondsmen, yet their funerals rival those of kings and marquises; in life and in death there is no restraint.

literal: They heap up lofty mounds and tombs, lavishly adorn sacrificial rites, and neighbors take pride in one another, calling it utmost filial piety.
idiomatic: They mound tombs sky-high and lavish ritual upon ritual; neighbors boast to one another and call it supreme filial piety.

literal: Moreover, the beginning of husband and wife is what royal transformation puts first; sharing food and joining the gourd are enough to complete the rites.
idiomatic: The bond of husband and wife is the first step in royal transformation; sharing a meal and drinking from one gourd are ceremony enough.

literal: Yet today's rich grow ever more extravagant: the arrangements for the joint wedding feast exceed sacrificial platters; fish are piled into mountains, the mountains have forest and trees, and atop the trees phoenixes perch.
idiomatic: Yet the rich grow ever more lavish: their joint-wedding feasts outdo sacrificial spreads — fish stacked into mountains, mountains planted with trees, and on the trees perch phoenixes.

literal: It is all toil for nothing; in the end it is cast away.
idiomatic: All is labor wasted; in the end it is thrown away.

literal: Looking up to Heaven's intent, it may not be so.
idiomatic: Surely Heaven's intent cannot be this.

literal: I ask that from now on, if weddings or funerals exceed the rites, they be judged as violating the edict.
idiomatic: I ask that hereafter, weddings or funerals that exceed proper rite be judged violations of the throne's intent.

literal: If officials do not investigate and impeach, they share the crime."
idiomatic: Officials who fail to investigate and impeach shall share the guilt."

literal: Xiaoyou accumulated years as mayor of Yin, held to the law himself, and won great repute; yet by nature he lacked backbone, was skilled at serving the powerful, and was mocked by the upright.
idiomatic: Xiaoyou held office in Yin for many years, kept to the law, and won great repute; yet he lacked backbone, was adept at courting the powerful, and upright men scorned him for it.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao of Qi, by precedent his rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linhuai county and appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: At the opening of Qi Tianbao, by precedent his rank was lowered; he was made duke of Linhuai county and appointed grand master for splendid happiness.

literal: In the winter of the second year he was summoned by edict into Jinyang Palace and, on leaving, was killed together with Yuan Huiye.
idiomatic: In the winter of the second year he was summoned by edict to Jinyang Palace; on leaving he was killed together with Yuan Huiye.

literal: Yuan Huiye, styled Shaoyuan, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Jingmu of Wei.
idiomatic: Yuan Huiye, styled Shaoyuan, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Jingmu of Wei.

literal: In youth he was crafty and mean, and often associated with bandits and robbers.
idiomatic: In youth he was mean and unscrupulous and kept company with bandits.

literal: When grown he changed his ways, studied the Masters and histories, was also rather skilled at composition, and was ardent in spirit and aspiration.
idiomatic: When grown he mended his ways, took up the Masters and histories, wrote passable prose, and bore himself with generous resolve.

literal: He rose through offices to Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, was given the supernumerary rank, headed the Secretariat Supervisor, and recorded affairs for the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He rose to minister of works and grand commandant, was given supernumerary rank, headed the secretariat, and recorded affairs for the masters of writing.

literal: Gao Cheng once asked him: "What are you perusing here?"
idiomatic: Gao Cheng once asked him, "What are you reading?"

literal: " He replied: "I often seek the biographies of Yi Yin and Huo Guang; I do not read the books of Cao [Cao] and the Sima [clan]."
idiomatic: " He replied, "I pore over the lives of Yi Yin and Huo Guang — not the chronicles of Cao Cao and the Sima clan."

literal: Huiye, seeing the times gradually decline, no longer plotted for survival; he devoted himself only to eating and drinking — one sheep a day, one calf every three days.
idiomatic: As the times waned, Huiye ceased to plot for his own survival; he gave himself only to eating and drinking — a sheep each day, a calf every three days.

literal: Again he once composed verse: "In old days we dwelt when the royal way was at peace, teeming with hosts of worthies;
idiomatic: He once composed verse: "In old days we dwelt when the royal way was at peace, teeming with hosts of worthies;

literal: Today we meet blocked roads in the world; foxes and hares throng the crossways."
idiomatic: Today the road is blocked; foxes and hares throng the crossways."

literal: At the beginning of Qi he was reduced in rank to Duke of Meiyang county, given the insignia Opening Office, Equal in Honor to the Three Offices, and made Supernumerary.
idiomatic: At the founding of Qi he was lowered to duke of Meiyang county, with opening office equal in honor to the three highest offices and supernumerary rank.

literal: While Huiye was at Jinyang he had no associations; in his usual leisure he composed the lineages of Wei imperial princes, titled "Records for Distinguishing Clans," forty juan, and it circulated in the world.
idiomatic: At Jinyang, Huiye kept to himself. In his leisure he compiled the genealogies of Wei's imperial princes under the title "Records for Distinguishing Clans," forty juan, and it circulated widely.

literal: His position and prestige were weighty; moreover, because his temperament was unlike others, he was often resented.
idiomatic: His rank and repute were weighty, yet his temperament set him apart and he was often resented.

literal: In the second year of Tianbao, following the imperial carriage to Jinyang, outside the palace gate he reviled Yuan Shao: "You are not equal to an old woman — you carried the seal on your back and gave it to another; why did you not smash it?
idiomatic: In Tianbao year two, while following the imperial carriage to Jinyang, he reviled Yuan Shao outside the palace gate: "You are worse than an old crone — you bore the seal on your back and handed it to another. Why not have smashed it?

literal: I speak these words knowing I shall die — yet how much longer will you have!"
idiomatic: I speak this knowing I shall die — but how much longer will you last?"

literal: When Gao Yang heard of it he had him killed and also beheaded Duke of Linhuai Xiaoyou.
idiomatic: Gao Yang heard and had him killed; he also beheaded Duke of Linhuai Xiaoyou.

literal: Facing execution, Xiaoyou was panic-stricken and at a loss; Huiye's bearing was calm.
idiomatic: At the block Xiaoyou panicked; Huiye's bearing never changed.

literal: They then cut ice and sank their corpses.
idiomatic: Their bodies were sunk through holes cut in the ice.

literal: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye was quite learned and held the post of Grand Adviser.
idiomatic: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye was a scholar of some note and rose to grand adviser.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang visited the south of Luo, Zhaoye stood outside the Changhe Gate, seized the horse's bridle, and remonstrated; the emperor avoided him and passed by, but later commended and encouraged him.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang visited south Luo, Zhaoye stood outside Changhe Gate, seized the bridle, and remonstrated. The emperor avoided him and rode on, but later commended him.

literal: He rose to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, General of the Guard, and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and died.
idiomatic: He rose to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, general of the guard, and right grand master for splendid happiness, and died.

literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Wen.
idiomatic: His posthumous title was Marquis Cultured.

literal: Yuan Bi, styled Fuzong, was son of Hui, Minister of Works of Wei.
idiomatic: Yuan Bi, styled Fuzong, was son of Hui, minister of works of Wei.

literal: By nature he was firm and upright and possessed literary learning.
idiomatic: By nature he was upright and learned.

literal: He held the post of Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He held the post of regular attendant.

literal: As heir of the main line he should have inherited his predecessor's enfeoffment.
idiomatic: As heir of the main line he should have inherited the family enfeoffment.

literal: But his younger uncle Li, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, through the Yu clan's favor in kinship, thereupon seized Bi's princely rank and arbitrarily granted it to his elder uterine brother's son Dan; Bi then abandoned human affairs, feigned illness, and returned to his private residence.
idiomatic: His uncle Li, vice director of the masters of writing, used the Yu clan's favor at court to strip Bi of his princely rank and grant it to his uterine brother's son Dan. Bi thereupon withdrew from public life, pleaded illness, and retired to his private residence.

literal: In Xuanwu's time he was made Palace Attendant; Bi submitted a memorial firmly declining.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was made palace attendant; Bi submitted a memorial firmly declining.

literal: He entered Mount Song, took a cave for his chamber, wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, and died.
idiomatic: He entered Mount Song, made a cave his home, wore hemp and ate greens, and died.

literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely rank.
idiomatic: In Jianyuan year one his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely rank.

literal: In the third year of Yong'an, posthumously he was given Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous title Wenxian.
idiomatic: In Yong'an year three he was posthumously made director of the masters of writing and duke of the department of state affairs, with the posthumous title Cultured and Offering.

literal: Earlier, Bi once dreamed that someone told him: "Your person will not transmit the enfeoffment of the age; he who will continue the former rank is your eldest son Shaoyuan."
idiomatic: Earlier Bi had dreamed that someone told him, "You will not pass the enfeoffment down in your own lifetime; your eldest son Shaoyuan will restore the former rank."

literal: When Bi awoke he at once told Huiye, and in the end it was as spoken.
idiomatic: When Bi awoke he told Huiye at once, and in the end it proved true.

literal: Shao by nature and conduct was mild and generous; as son-in-law of the Gao clan he enjoyed considerable favor of the times.
idiomatic: Shao was mild and generous by nature; as a son-in-law of the Gaos he enjoyed considerable favor.

literal: He could humble himself and yield; in governing men he had policies of kindness.
idiomatic: He knew how to yield; in office he governed with kindness.

literal: He loved Confucian learning and with ritual received men of talent.
idiomatic: He loved Confucian learning and with proper ceremony welcomed men of talent.

literal: He loved forests and springs, built mansions and residences — splendid yet not extravagant.
idiomatic: He loved forests and springs and built mansions splendid but not extravagant.

literal: Gao Yang shaved Shao's beard and whiskers, applied powder and rouge, dressed him in women's garments to keep at his side, saying: "I take Pengcheng as my palace woman."
idiomatic: Gao Yang shaved Shao's beard, painted his face, dressed him in women's clothes and kept him at his side, saying, "I take Prince of Pengcheng as my consort."

literal: He mocked the weakness of the Yuan clan, comparing them to women.
idiomatic: He mocked the Yuan for their weakness, likening them to women.

literal: In the tenth year, the Grand Astrologer memorialized: "This year old shall be removed and new spread."
idiomatic: In year ten the grand astrologer reported, "This year the old must yield to the new."

literal: Gao Yang said to Shao: "Why did Han Guangwu restore the dynasty?"
idiomatic: Gao Yang asked Shao, "Why did Emperor Guangwu of Han restore the dynasty?"

literal: Shao said: "Because the Liu were not all killed."
idiomatic: Shao said, "Because the Liu were not all killed."

literal: Thereupon they killed the various Yuan to satisfy the omen.
idiomatic: Thereupon they slaughtered the Yuan to satisfy the omen.

literal: Then in the fifth month they executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; the remaining nineteen households were all placed under restraint.
idiomatic: In the fifth month they executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; the remaining nineteen households were all placed under restraint.

literal: Shao was imprisoned in the capital-district dungeon, denied food, and died gnawing his sleeves.
idiomatic: Shao was imprisoned in the capital dungeon, denied food, and died gnawing his sleeves.

literal: By the seventh month came the great slaughter of the Yuan; from Zhaocheng down, none were spared.
idiomatic: By the seventh month came the great slaughter of the Yuan; from Emperor Zhaocheng down, none were spared.

literal: Some had fathers or grandfathers who were kings, some had themselves long held high rank, some had brothers in their prime — all were beheaded at the Eastern Market.
idiomatic: Some had fathers or grandfathers who had been kings, some had themselves long held high rank, some had brothers in their prime — all were beheaded at the Eastern Market.

literal: Their infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.
idiomatic: Their infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.

literal: In all, before and after, seven hundred twenty-one died; all corpses were cast into the Zhang River. When fish were gutted many claws and nails were found; for a long time the capital would not eat fish.
idiomatic: Seven hundred twenty-one died in all; every corpse was cast into the Zhang River. When fish were gutted, claws and nails were found inside; for a long time the capital would not eat fish.

literal: The encomium says: The Yuan clan flourished in abundance, relying on this auspicious numen.
idiomatic: Encomium: The Yuan clan flourished in full vigor, blessed by fate's favor.

literal: The Way followed the ending fortune; their fate met wanton punishment.
idiomatic: The Way waned with the dynasty's end; their lives met cruel and lawless punishment.

literal: The complete text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
